name: Lateral-thinking yes/no puzzle
aliases: ask yes or no questions to solve it
summary: Read a strange short story, type yes/no questions in your own words and get Yes, No or Doesn't matter until you can explain what really happened; fewer questions scores more.
core_loop: read the odd setup → type a yes/no question → see which question was answered and the reply → collect clues → type your theory and tap Solve
rules: each answered question costs one of a fixed budget; unclear questions cost nothing
answers come from a fact bank written when the game is made, never improvised
a wrong solution costs extra questions
solving scores more the fewer questions you used
win: explain the story before the questions run out
scoring: solve bonus plus points per question left, plus points per key clue found
social_hooks: the Group gets the same daily story and compares how few questions each needed
share your best question without spoiling the answer
content_needs: cases: setup, hidden solution, 30-60 facts with replies and the words players use, solutions (qa-bank/1, refined once)
difficulty_levers: how far the story is from the obvious reading
example_prompts: lateral thinking puzzles where I ask yes/no questions to solve them
a man walks into a bar and asks for water style riddles
black stories game for our group chat
a daily situation puzzle where you ask yes or no questions
notes: Kevin32 #26. Typed on the iPhone keyboard (qa_bank v2 brings a native text field); the matcher answers about 90% of held-out player questions right after one refine round (docs/harness-gaps/open-text.md).

name: Interrogate by typed questions
aliases: type my own question to the suspect
summary: A suspect or witness answers your typed yes/no questions from what they know (and lie about); find the contradiction and name the culprit or the truth.
core_loop: read the case → type a question to the character → get yes, no or a dodge → spot what doesn't fit → type the accusation and tap Solve
rules: the character's answers come from a written fact bank, with partly for evasive answers
each answered question costs time or a question
the accusation must name the key facts
win: name the culprit and how before the questions run out
scoring: solve bonus plus points per question left
social_hooks: friends race the same case and compare question counts
content_needs: one case per run: setup, hidden truth, facts in the character's knowledge, solutions (qa-bank/1)
example_prompts: interrogate a suspect by typing my own questions
detective game where I question the butler
ask the witness anything and catch the lie
notes: For picking from written questions instead, use the existing interrogation types (choice_story).

name: Character rates your line
summary: A character says something; pick the best of a few replies and they rate it from flop to legendary with a reaction; stack high ratings across the rounds.
core_loop: character says a line → pick one of 3 replies before the timer → see the 0-100 rating, its band and the reaction → next round
rules: every reply has a rating written when the game is made: one clearly best, one flop
a flop can cost a life
win: finish the rounds; the total rating is the score
scoring: sum of the ratings of the picked replies
social_hooks: compare rizz scores in the group chat
share the reply that got the best reaction
content_needs: rounds: the character's line, 3-4 replies, a rating and a reaction for each (npc_lines)
example_prompts: rizz simulator where I pick pickup lines and an NPC rates them from cringe to W rizz
flirt with the barista and see if she's impressed
notes: Kevin32 #23. Typing your own line and having it judged needs live_judge (a gap); the picked-reply version ships today. Real names are used as the person wrote them; portraits are drawn caricatures, never photorealistic.

name: Convince the gatekeeper
summary: A bouncer, guard or boss stands in your way; each round pick what to say and they rate how convinced they are, and a high enough total gets you in.
core_loop: gatekeeper objects → pick a reply → see how convinced they are and their comeback → next objection → in or out
rules: each reply has a written rating and comeback
a total over the bar gets you in; flops cost patience
win: total rating over the bar after the last objection
lose: patience runs out after too many flops
social_hooks: see which friends got in and with what line
content_needs: objections with 3 replies each, ratings and comebacks (npc_lines)
example_prompts: convince the bouncer to let me into the club
talk your way past the castle guard
persuade my boss to give me friday off
